newsitem.title: USA: Japan stock drop no threat to US-Commerce official.
newsitem.headline: Japan stock drop no threat to US-Commerce official.

text.p: The recent steep fall in the Tokyo stock market does not pose a threat to the U.S. economy, but it needs to be watched closely, Commerce Undersecretary Everett Ehrlich said on Tuesday.
"I don't think there's an immediate threat to the United States posed by recent events in Japan," he told Reuters.
But he added that the Japanese economy was sufficiently integrated into the world economy that developments there needed to be monitored "very carefully."
The benchmark Nikkei average of 225 leading shares closed 25.66 points lower on Tuesday at 18,093.13. The index lost 2,000 points last week.
Some analysts have blamed the price drop on Tokyo's plans for a "Big Bang" reform of financial markets.
But Ehrlich argued that the market's fall was "emblematic" of Japan's structural problems and resulted from its too slow, rather than its too rapid, reform efforts.
The Japanese government has tried to boost its economy through monetary and fiscal stimulus, but neither has worked. The answer is structural reforms, Ehrlich argued.
